mermaidTitle: Three keys, three jobs - CCAR-F study workbench
mermaidCaption: You learn Claude Code and the Claude API; this app's own demos ran on Gemini. (Diagram as it was in the Streamlit app.)
whatIs: **What the certification tests.** The official exam guide (v1.0, CCAR-F) says the Claude Certified Architect – Foundations exam validates that practitioners can make informed decisions about tradeoffs when implementing real-world solutions with Claude, across **Claude Code**, the **Claude Agent SDK**, the **Claude API**, and **MCP**. Questions are scenario-based, drawn from 4 of a published bank of 6 production contexts, and test judgment and architecture decisions, not trivia.

**Why the Streamlit app's demos ran on Gemini, not the Claude API.** The user chose Gemini for the live demos on cost grounds: it was the same setup as the earlier `agents101` project, and cheap enough to run every pattern demo freely while studying. That was a deliberate trade-off, with one consequence worth being honest about: **a Gemini demo shows the *pattern* the exam is testing, not Claude's exact fields.** Where Gemini says `function_call`, Claude says `tool_use`; where Gemini has a function-calling *mode*, Claude has `tool_choice`.

**Where the real Claude API came back in.** A handful of pages, flagged with a key icon in the phase tables, teach mechanics that only the real Claude API can show honestly (the exact `stop_reason` loop, the three `tool_choice` modes, structured output via `tool_use`, Message Batches). Those pages were to use the real Claude API and remind the learner to buy a small, capped key before reaching them. Everywhere else, Claude Code itself, the tool used in the VS Code panel, runs on the **subscription**, with no API key involved at all.

keyNotes: Claude Code runs on your subscription. There is no API key to find or protect for it, and it is separate from any app key.

`.env.example` documents the two app keys: `GEMINI_API_KEY` ("needed ONLY for live demos that call Gemini from Python"; key from Google AI Studio) and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` ("needed for the flagged pages. BUY BEFORE DAY 1 of the study plan"; bought in the Claude Console, with a low spend limit). Both were placeholders only (`your_api_key_here`); real values lived in the local, gitignored `.env`.

firstCall.intro: The page made one plain, single-turn call to Gemini 2.5 Flash with the question "What does the CCAR-F exam test, in one sentence?". Examples only: this code is not runnable here.
firstCall.code1Label: Example (not runnable here): the core pattern from the page
firstCall.code1:
from google import genai

client   = genai.Client(api_key=GEMINI_API_KEY)
response = client.models.generate_content(
    model="gemini-2.5-flash",
    contents="What does CCAR-F test, in one sentence?",
)
print(response.text)
firstCall.wrapper: `utils/llm.py` wrapped this call: it loaded the key, built the client, retried on transient 503s (4 attempts, exponential backoff 3 to 20 seconds), and returned plain text. Every page imported the same `chat()` function; to swap the model you changed one line (`MODEL = "gemini-2.5-flash"`) in that one file. When the first key-icon page was to be built, a `CLAUDE_MODEL` constant was to be added right next to it using the real `anthropic` SDK, a second wrapper beside it, not a replacement. If the key was missing, `_client()` raised `GEMINI_API_KEY not set. Copy .env.example to .env and add your key.`

firstCall.whatHappened: That call went to **Gemini 2.5 Flash**, through `utils/llm.py`, the same wrapper every later page used. The Execution Trace showed the finish reason Gemini actually returned, with the Claude term it maps to written beside it. That side-by-side habit is how every starred page stayed honest about which product it was really demonstrating.

principles: **Works without a key.** No key must not break the app. Pure-Python demos and quizzes worked without one. A demo that called Gemini showed a clear "needs GEMINI_API_KEY" message when there was none.
**SIMULATED is always labelled.** If a page offered a simulated fallback, it was labelled SIMULATED on screen and in the trace. Simulated output was never presented as a real model response.
**Never hide an API failure.** Errors were shown, not swallowed behind a default value.

**Never show a key.** Real keys never appear in code, logs, traces or UI output (the page itself showed only a masked fragment of the Gemini key when loaded; the project later tightened that rule to forbid even partial display).
